note.explanation: A chemical formula tells you which atoms or ions are present and the ratio in which they occur. For a molecule, the formula shows the types and numbers of atoms in one molecule.
examples: H₂O means that one water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
NaCl shows a 1:1 ratio of sodium ions to chloride ions in the ionic compound.
note.checkAnswer: H₂O means two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in one molecule.
note.simple: A formula is a short way to show what a substance is made of. Small numbers show how many atoms are present.
note.checkQuestion: What does the formula H₂O show about one water molecule?
note.title: Reading chemical formulae
steps: Read the element symbols in the formula.
Use each small number to count the atoms of the symbol just before it.
If there is no small number, that element has one atom.
For an ionic compound, the formula unit shows the simplest ratio of its ions.
note.answer: A chemical formula shows the types of atoms in a substance and, where indicated, their numbers or simplest ratio.

options: One nitrogen atom and one hydrogen atom
One nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms
Three nitrogen atoms and one hydrogen atom
Three nitrogen atoms and three hydrogen atoms
mcqs.stem: What does the formula NH₃ show about one molecule of ammonia?
rationales: This is incorrect because the subscript 3 applies to hydrogen, not nitrogen.
This is correct because N has no subscript and H has the subscript 3.
This is incorrect because the formula has no subscript 3 after N.
This is incorrect because the formula shows only one nitrogen atom.
This represents one oxygen atom, not an ozone molecule.
This represents a molecule containing two oxygen atoms.
This is correct because an ozone molecule contains three oxygen atoms.
This would represent four oxygen atoms, not ozone.

mcqs.stem: Sodium chloride contains sodium and chloride ions in a 1:1 ratio. Which is its formula unit?
rationales: This is correct because NaCl shows the simplest 1:1 ratio.
This is incorrect because it shows two sodium ions for each chloride ion.
This is incorrect because it shows two chloride ions for each sodium ion.
This is not the simplest ratio; it reduces to NaCl.

mcqs.stem: Calcium chloride has one calcium ion for every two chloride ions. Which is its formula?
rationales: This does not show the required two chloride ions.
This is correct because it shows one calcium for every two chlorides.
This gives the wrong ratio of calcium to chloride.
This is not the simplest ratio; it reduces to CaCl.

options: The number and type of atoms in one molecule
The mass of one molecule in grams
The number of molecules in one gram
The simplest ratio of ions in every compound
mcqs.stem: What does a molecular formula show?
rationales: This is correct: a molecular formula shows the types and numbers of atoms in one molecule.
This describes a mass, not what the molecular formula represents.
This is a particle-count idea, not the definition of a molecular formula.
This describes a formula unit ratio for ionic compounds, not every compound's molecular formula.

mcqs.stem: Which formula represents an ionic compound as a formula unit?
rationales: This is the molecular formula of a covalent compound.
This is correct because sodium chloride is an ionic compound represented by a formula unit.
This is a formula for a molecule of an element.
This is the molecular formula of a covalent compound.

mcqs.stem: Which formula shows a compound made of ions in a 1:2 ratio?
rationales: This molecular formula shows one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms.
This molecular formula shows two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
This is correct because CaCl₂ shows one calcium for every two chloride ions.
This molecular formula shows one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms.

mcqs.stem: Which formula shows two hydrogen atoms bonded with two oxygen atoms in one molecule?
rationales: This is correct because the subscripts show two hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms.
This shows two hydrogen atoms but only one oxygen atom.
This shows one hydrogen atom and two oxygen atoms.
This shows four hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

written.text: How would you differentiate between the chemical formula of an element and that of a compound? Give examples. Write down the names of ionic and covalent compounds whose formulas have been given in this article.
written.finalAnswer: An element's formula contains only one kind of atom, for example Na, Ca, C, Fe, O₂, N₂, H₂ and O₃. A compound's formula contains two or more kinds of atoms, for example NaCl, CaCl₂, KBr, BaCl₂, H₂O, NH₃ and CH₄. Ionic compounds: sodium chloride (NaCl), calcium chloride (CaCl₂), potassium bromide (KBr) and barium chloride (BaCl₂). Covalent compounds: water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃), methane (CH₄), hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen fluoride (HF), hydrogen sulphide (H₂S), phosphine (PH₃), hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄), carbon dioxide (CO₂), carbon monoxide (CO) and benzene (C₆H₆).

rubric.why: This states the key difference for an element.
rubric.description: Describe the formula of an element and give examples.
rubric.how: State that an element's formula contains only one kind of atom and give examples such as Na or O₂.

accept: two or more kinds of atoms
rubric.why: This states the key difference for a compound.
rubric.description: Describe the formula of a compound and give examples.
rubric.how: State that a compound's formula contains different kinds of atoms and give examples.

rubric.why: Naming the ionic examples shows that the given formulae have been identified correctly.
rubric.description: Name the ionic compounds given in the article.
rubric.how: Name the ionic compounds, including sodium chloride, calcium chloride, potassium bromide and barium chloride.

rubric.why: The final marks are for correctly naming the covalent compounds in the article.
rubric.description: Name the covalent compounds given in the article.
rubric.how: Give the names corresponding to the listed covalent formulae, such as water, ammonia, methane, hydrogen chloride and carbon dioxide.

modelAnswer: An element's formula contains only one kind of atom; examples are Na, Ca, C, Fe, O₂, N₂, H₂ and O₃.
A compound's formula contains two or more kinds of atoms; examples are NaCl, CaCl₂, KBr, BaCl₂, H₂O, NH₃ and CH₄.
Ionic compounds: NaCl is sodium chloride; CaCl₂ is calcium chloride; KBr is potassium bromide; BaCl₂ is barium chloride.

Covalent compounds: H₂O is water; NH₃ is ammonia; CH₄ is methane; HCl is hydrogen chloride; HF is hydrogen fluoride; H₂S is hydrogen sulphide; PH₃ is phosphine; H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide; H₂SO₄ is sulphuric acid; CO₂ is carbon dioxide; CO is carbon monoxide; C₆H₆ is benzene.

written.text: Write down the chemical formula of barium nitride.

rubric.why: The correct element symbols are needed to form the compound formula.
rubric.description: Identify the symbols for barium and nitrogen.
rubric.how: Write Ba for barium and N for nitride.

rubric.why: The final formula must show the correct simplest ratio.
rubric.description: Give the correct formula.
rubric.how: Write Ba₃N₂ as the final formula.

modelAnswer: Barium forms Ba²⁺ ions and nitride forms N³⁻ ions.
The simplest ratio that balances the charges is 3 Ba²⁺ ions to 2 N³⁻ ions.
The formula is Ba₃N₂.

written.text: Find out the molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH₂O and its molar mass is 180.

rubric.why: The empirical formula mass is needed to find the multiplier.
rubric.description: Calculate the empirical formula mass.
rubric.how: Add the relative atomic masses for CH₂O to obtain 30.

rubric.why: The multiplier determines how many empirical formula units are in the molecular formula.
rubric.description: Find the multiplier.
rubric.how: Divide the molar mass by the empirical formula mass: 180 ÷ 30 = 6.

rubric.why: The correct final formula applies the multiplier to every subscript.
rubric.description: Give the molecular formula.
rubric.how: Multiply every subscript in CH₂O by 6 and state C₆H₁₂O₆.

modelAnswer: Empirical formula mass of CH₂O = 12 + (2 × 1) + 16 = 30.
Multiplier = molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass = 180 ÷ 30 = 6.
Molecular formula = (CH₂O)₆.
The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.

written.text: Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: Different compounds may have the same empirical formula because it gives only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, not the actual number of atoms in a molecule. Different molecular formulae can reduce to the same empirical formula. A molecular formula identifies the actual number and types of atoms in one molecule, so different compounds do not have the same molecular formula.

rubric.why: This explains what an empirical formula represents.
rubric.description: Explain what the empirical formula shows.
rubric.how: State that it shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

rubric.why: This distinguishes an empirical formula from a molecular formula.
rubric.description: Explain why compounds can share an empirical formula.
rubric.how: Explain that different actual atom counts can reduce to the same simplest ratio.

rubric.why: The molecular formula represents the actual atoms in an individual molecule.
rubric.description: Describe what a molecular formula shows.
rubric.how: State that it gives the types and actual numbers of atoms in one molecule.

accept: different compounds do not have the same molecular formula
rubric.why: The final response must directly address both parts of the claim.
rubric.description: State the conclusion clearly.
rubric.how: Conclude that compounds may share an empirical formula but have different molecular formulae.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of the different atoms in a molecule.
Different actual numbers of atoms can reduce to the same simplest ratio, so different compounds can have the same empirical formula.
A molecular formula shows the actual number and types of atoms in one molecule.
Therefore, different compounds may have the same empirical formula but have different molecular formulae.

written.text: Write down the chemical formulas of the following compounds. Calcium phosphate, Aluminium nitride, Sodium acetate, Ammonium carbonate and Bismuth sulphate.
written.finalAnswer: Calcium phosphate: Ca₃(PO₄)₂; Aluminium nitride: AlN; Sodium acetate: CH₃COONa; Ammonium carbonate: (NH₄)₂CO₃; Bismuth sulphate: Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

rubric.why: The first pair checks correct formula writing for ionic compounds.
rubric.description: Give the formulae of calcium phosphate and aluminium nitride.
rubric.how: Write Ca₃(PO₄)₂ and AlN.

rubric.why: The sodium acetate formula must preserve the acetate group.
rubric.description: Give the formula of sodium acetate.
rubric.how: Write CH₃COONa.

rubric.why: Parentheses and the subscript are needed for the ammonium ion ratio.
rubric.description: Give the formula of ammonium carbonate.
rubric.how: Write (NH₄)₂CO₃.

rubric.why: The sulphate group and its subscript must be shown correctly.
rubric.description: Give the formula of bismuth sulphate.
rubric.how: Write Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

rubric.why: The final mark is for presenting the complete set of correct formulae.
rubric.description: Check and present all five formulae.
rubric.how: Ensure every listed compound has its correct formula.

modelAnswer: Calcium phosphate: Ca₃(PO₄)₂.
Aluminium nitride: AlN.
Sodium acetate: CH₃COONa.
Ammonium carbonate: (NH₄)₂CO₃.
Bismuth sulphate: Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

written.text: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: Sand has a giant structure rather than separate SiO₂ molecules. Its formula, SiO₂, represents the simplest 1:2 ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms in the structure, so it is a formula unit.

rubric.why: Recognising the structure explains why the formula is not a molecule count.
rubric.description: Describe the structure of sand.
rubric.how: State that sand does not consist of separate SiO₂ molecules.

rubric.why: The atom ratio is the basis of the formula.
rubric.description: Give the silicon-to-oxygen ratio.
rubric.how: State that the simplest ratio is one silicon atom to two oxygen atoms.

rubric.why: This explains how the formula is obtained for a giant ionic or network structure.
rubric.description: Explain what SiO₂ represents.
rubric.how: Explain that SiO₂ shows the simplest whole-number ratio in the structure.

rubric.why: The correct final formula is required.
rubric.description: State the formula of sand.
rubric.how: Give SiO₂ as the formula.

modelAnswer: Sand does not exist as separate SiO₂ molecules; it has a giant structure.
The atoms in the structure occur in the simplest ratio of one silicon atom to two oxygen atoms.
Therefore, SiO₂ is the formula unit showing this simplest ratio.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask you to write a formula or distinguish the formula of an element from that of a compound.
For formula-writing questions, show the correct element symbols, subscripts and brackets around repeated groups of atoms.
For an explanation, state what the formula represents and give an example; this helps secure the explanation marks.
When a question asks what a molecular formula shows, mention both the types and the actual numbers of atoms in one molecule.

explain.title: Formulae of elements
explain.body: Some elements are represented by their symbols alone, such as Na, Ca, C and Fe. Other elements exist as molecules: oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are O₂, N₂ and H₂, and ozone is O₃.

explain.title: Formulae of ionic compounds
explain.body: Ionic compounds are represented by formula units. A formula unit shows the minimum ratio between the ions. For example, NaCl shows a 1:1 ratio, while CaCl₂ shows one calcium ion for every two chloride ions.

explain.title: Molecular formulae
explain.body: Covalent compounds generally exist as discrete molecules. A chemical compound is represented by a chemical formula which is called the molecular formula of that compound and which shows all the types of atoms bonded together in one molecule of that compound. For example, H₂O shows two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

explain.title: Empirical formulae and ratios
explain.body: The empirical formula of a compound is the simplest whole number ratio of different atoms in a molecule. It may not show the actual number of atoms in one molecule, so different molecular formulae can reduce to the same empirical formula.

mistakes: Do not forget that a missing subscript means one atom.
Do not apply a subscript to the wrong element; in NH₃, the 3 applies only to hydrogen.
Do not write an ionic formula with a ratio that can still be simplified; a formula unit shows the minimum ratio.
When a group of atoms occurs more than once, use brackets, as in (NH₄)₂CO₃.
Do not confuse a molecular formula, which gives actual atoms in one molecule, with an empirical formula, which gives only the simplest ratio.
